question: What is the primary purpose of performing last offices in a clinical setting?

options.A: Preparing the body immediately for an autopsy procedure
options.B: Preserving the dignity of the deceased and supporting relatives
options.C: Disinfecting the hospital room for the next incoming admission
options.D: Fulfilling mandatory legal requirements for immediate burial

explanation: Last offices focus primarily on maintaining respect for the person who has passed away while offering comfort to those left behind. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why is formal medical verification of death required before beginning last offices?

options.A: To immediately release the medical insurance bond to the family
options.B: To calculate the exact time required for mortuary staff arrival
options.C: To prevent premature post-mortem procedures on living patients
options.D: To determine which religious rites should be performed first

explanation: A physician must officially confirm death to ensure there is no chance of accidental intervention while a patient is still alive. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: What action must be taken immediately when a patient dies under suspicious or unexplained circumstances?

options.A: Report the case to hospital administration and authorities before proceeding
options.B: Complete standard last offices and transfer the body directly home
options.C: Disinfect the personal belongings and hand them to local security
options.D: Obtain immediate verbal consent from the next of kin for an autopsy

explanation: Sudden or suspicious deaths fall under coroner laws, requiring official notification before the body is disturbed or prepared. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: How should a nurse handle conflicting cultural or religious requests regarding post-mortem care?

options.A: Refuse all outside requests to maintain strict hospital standardization
options.B: Insist that hospital policy always supersedes any personal belief system
options.C: Delay all nursing procedures until legal counsel reviews the case file
options.D: Accommodate the requests as long as public health and safety rules permit

explanation: Culturally sensitive nursing requires balancing family traditions with professional safety standards whenever feasible. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential when performing last offices?

options.A: N95 respirators for every routine procedure
options.B: Lead aprons to block potential radiation exposure
options.C: Heavy-duty utility boots and sterile gowns

explanation: Standard barrier precautions like gloves and aprons protect the nurse from exposure to residual body fluids. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for packing natural orifices with cotton wool during post-mortem care?

options.A: To prevent the leakage of bodily fluids and maintain hygiene
options.B: To block unpleasant odors from escaping during the transfer
options.C: To absorb external moisture in humid mortuary environments
options.D: To alter facial contours back to a lifelike resting appearance

explanation: Packing orifices stops post-mortem purging, protecting the environment and those handling the body from contamination. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: Why is a small pillow placed under the head of the deceased during positioning?

options.A: To prevent pooling of blood and discoloration in the face
options.B: To elevate the upper body above the level of the heart
options.C: To make the facial features look relaxed for viewing relatives
options.D: To keep the jaw securely closed without using chin straps

explanation: Elevating the head slightly with a small pillow stops gravitational pooling of blood, which causes facial discoloration. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: When should the positioning phase of last offices ideally be completed?

options.A: Immediately following the family's viewing session
options.B: Once the death certificate has been signed by a registrar
options.C: Before the onset of rigor mortis stiffens the joints
options.D: After the mortuary attendants arrive to collect the body

explanation: Positioning must be done promptly while the muscles are still pliable, before rigor mortis makes limb movement difficult. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: Who should ideally witness the inventory and cataloging of a deceased patient's valuables?

options.A: The mortuary attendant receiving the body
options.B: The attending physician who certified the death
options.C: A local community leader or religious elder
options.D: Another healthcare worker or security officer

explanation: Having a second staff member witness the inventory protects against accusations of theft and ensures accountability. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is the correct protocol when a deceased patient has valuable personal effects and no family is present?

options.A: Hand the belongings over to the local police department immediately
options.B: Deposit the items in the hospital safe and note the receipt
options.C: Store the items inside the bedside locker until the family visits
options.D: Keep the valuables in the nurse's station drawer for safekeeping

explanation: Unclaimed valuables must go into secure institutional storage according to facility protocol to ensure legal protection. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which document must accompany the deceased body during transfer to the hospital mortuary?

options.A: Complete patient history from admission to discharge
options.B: Mortuary slip and matching identification details
options.C: Financial clearance certificate from the billing office
options.D: Original prescription charts and diagnostic lab results

explanation: The mortuary slip and secure identification tags ensure safe handover and prevent mix-ups at the morgue. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why should the transport trolley be covered when moving a deceased patient through hospital corridors?

options.A: To maintain privacy and prevent distress to others
options.B: To protect the shroud from gathering dust and lint
options.C: To keep the body temperature from rising during transit
options.D: To comply with federal quarantine and hygiene laws

explanation: Covering the trolley shows respect for the deceased and spares patients and visitors unnecessary emotional upset. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)
